body:
Opening the first thread froze the board for 6 to 7 seconds, then 3 more. The fix is a one-rule CSS change on branch worktree-cl12 (ccd7d52 = main + the fix); the live page needs a republish.

## Which build has it
Both: the live page (v39) and kit main (0ce9353), reproduced in Chromium with a copy of your Artifact's data (Harmonize and the kit board). On the kit board, opening the first thread in Ask the orchestrator blocked the page 6.8 s, then 2.9 s. A post opens the same way when its comments nest deep.

## Cause
Each reply is drawn inside the one it answers, and those boxes were CSS grids, one inside the other. A grid sizes its items more than once, so the cost multiplied with each level. Your first kit-board thread is 6 replies deep: one layout of the orchestrator window took 6.3 s (Chrome trace), and the "New below" pill forced that layout on open. It hit the first thread because it is the newest, and the deepest.

## Fix
Threads and replies are plain block boxes; the space between replies is a margin. Same look. On your data: 6.8 s to 3 ms.

## Test
`kit/board/test_page_speed.js` (in run_all_tests): a thread 7 replies deep, in the orchestrator window and as a post's comments, at desktop and phone widths, must open in under 1 s. On main the page is still frozen after 5 s; with the fix it opens in 6 to 25 ms.
breaks: sed -i 's/^\.node { display: block; }/.node { display: grid; }/; s/border-left: 2px solid var(--line); display: block; }/border-left: 2px solid var(--line); display: grid; }/' kit/board/board.template.html && node kit/board/test_page_speed.js  (fails: frozen after 5 s; git checkout the file after)

title: Opening the first thread or post no longer freezes the board
verdict: The freeze was nested CSS grids for reply threads (6 levels cost 6 s per layout); now block boxes: 6.8 s to 3 ms on his data, with a test that fails on main.
